sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Bruneck is reshaping its centre around underground garages and a pedestrian town. The 2020 traffic concept plans to move above-ground parking into underground garages and to create a new pedestrian zone around Herzog-Sigmund-Strasse; it expects about 1,700 public spaces to be served in future from a new Stegener Marktplatz access, including 350 at the Rathaus garage, 300 at the NOI Techpark garage and 340 at the mobility centre [0]. A general driving ban has applied on the whole of Europastrasse behind the town hall since February 2024; the police counted 178 violations in the first month and recommended the Rathaus and NOBIS garages [3]. In April 2024 the town executive approved a land-use change for the Bruneck Ost mobility concept, which still needed council approval, with an underground garage at the Schlosswiese with 250 public spaces and a 69 percent cut in motorised traffic in Bruneck Ost [4]. A 30 km/h limit has applied across the urban area since June 2026, and the Graben is closed to private traffic during events while the town assesses the effects [14].

For developers the town charges a payment in lieu of 25,000 euros per missing space for 2025, adjusted yearly [6]. Surface parking follows a directive amended on 23 February 2026: zones A to C charge Monday to Friday 8:00 to 19:00 and Saturday 8:00 to 13:00, with 1.80 euros an hour and a 90-minute maximum in zone A, 3.00 euros in A2, and Stegener Marktplatz (zone D) at 1.00 euro an hour and a 5 euro day rate every day [10]. The stated aims are to minimise parking-search traffic, discourage all-day parking in the centre and steer drivers to free and fringe car parks [11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The station mobility centre opened on 16 June 2022, a project of about 7.5 million euros coordinated by the South Tyrol transport company, with the car park reached by a tunnel from Stegener Marktplatz [2]. In 2020 the first phase had been announced as 230 car spaces and a new bus terminal [1]. A 2025 audit under the Interreg ParkPAD project listed Bruneck's own challenges from stakeholder talks: short-stay zones should be used more, surface car parks reduced in favour of underground ones, and the planned Schlosswiese garage was seen as not ideal [5]. In April 2026 the municipality offered private persons and companies spaces in the Parking NOBIS garage at the NOI Techpark [13]. Municipal lists show 6 electric-vehicle spaces at the mobility centre, 8 at NOBIS and 2 charging stations at the northern fringe car park, and an annual permit of 120 euros for electric vehicles of people working or living in Bruneck [12]. For Kronplatz, parking at the Reischach valley station is chargeable while that at Olang is free [15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The town runs its garages itself. The council amended the rules for Parking Rathaus, NOBIS and the Gilm garage on 4 February 2026; the municipal police run all three, Gilm takes annual subscribers only, and exit is free within 20 minutes of entry [7]. From 10 February 2026 the Rathaus garage introduced 30 free minutes [8]; the two texts differ on the free period. The municipal list of March 2026 gives Parking Rathaus 354 spaces at 1.80 euros an hour on weekdays, NOBIS 292 at 1.60 euros, the hospital garage 228 at 2.00 euros and the mobility centre 220 at 1.00 euro with the first 60 minutes free [9].

Our data cover four car parks with 1,188 spaces from the South Tyrol open-data platform, measured since 27 September 2026, and show them very little used. Weighted by spaces, occupancy averaged about 16% on weekdays and 9% at weekends. The feed's Centro Città (361 spaces) and the hospital car park (209) are the fullest, at 24% and 25% on weekdays, and the hospital reached 87% in one weekday-morning reading. The NOBIS garage (378 in the feed against 292 in the municipal list) averaged 6%, and the mobility centre (240 against 220) 11%, so the garages that the town recommends and that the concept counts on are mostly empty. This is about three weeks of data in early autumn, outside the peak seasons.
